text: Conversion Cost with Uncertainties, $/Diesel Gallon Equivalent (DGE) (in 2020 USD) The uncertainties in MFSPs and conversion costs of soybean-derived BD and RD are comparatively low. For instance, the 25th to 75th percentile range for the MFSP of soybean oil to BD is $3.17 to $3.67 per DGE, with a median of $3.36 per DGE. Similarly, the 25th to 75th percentile range for the MFSP of soybean oil to RD is $3.62 to $4.20 per DGE, with a median of $3.86 per DGE. The 25th to 75th percentile ranges for conversion costs are $0.51 to $0.57 per DGE for BD, and $0.54 to $0.81 per DGE for RD. As anticipated, there is minimal uncertainty associated with conversion costs for higher TRL pathways, while fluctuations in soybean oil prices are the primary driver of uncertainty in MFSP. In contrast to the soybean oil to BD/RD pathways, the 25th to 75th percentile ranges for the MFSP of UCO to BD and RD are significantly higher: $4.80 to $6.00 per DGE and $4.73 to $6.14 per DGE, respectively. This is primarily due to fluctuations in UCO prices over the past few years. For the sludge and manure HTL to RD pathways, the 25th to 75th percentile ranges of MFSP are $3.19 to $3.87 per DGE for sludge and $4.18 to $4.85 per DGE for swine manure. For RD produced from biomass CFP with similar TRLs of 5–7, the 25th to 75th percentile ranges are $4.10 to $4.66 per DGE for MFSP and $2.56 to $3.00 per DGE for conversion cost. For both the HTL and CFP pathways, uncertainties in MFSP and conversion cost are primarily influenced by the primary conversion step (HTL or CFP) rather than the downstream upgrading of biocrude or bio- oil. The uncertainties for both MFSP and conversion costs exhibit similar trends for the gasification pathways that convert woody biomass to methanol and DME. This is primarily because the gasification process significantly affects the overall production costs while using the same feedstock. The 25th to 75th percentile ranges for the MFSP are $3.16 to $3.63 per DGE for woody biomass to methanol and $3.01 to $3.44 per DGE for woody biomass to DME. Note that nearly 70% of the uncertainty in MFSP is due to uncertainties in conversion costs; the remaining uncertainty stems from variations in feedstock prices. The uncertainties in MFSP for producing ethanol from corn stover are greater than those for corn starch. The 25th to 75th percentile range for the MFSP is $3.25 to $3.98 per DGE, with a median value of $3.60 per DGE. Fluctuations in feedstock prices account for most of this uncertainty. 9 MFSP exhibits the highest uncertainties among all 16 pathways for the two e-fuel pathways; the 25th to 75th percentile ranges are $6.84 to $9.81 per DGE for e-methanol and $6.14 to $8.54 per DGE for e-ammonia. The variation in green hydrogen prices is the most significant contributor to uncertainty. For e-ammonia, the uncertainty in conversion costs is only ± $0.02 per DGE, because the HB process is commercially available
